title: Hybrid admit controller: golden signals fusion and token-emission SLI dashboard
creator: Marisol Vega
description:
Goal: build a dashboard and telemetry plumbing that fuses golden signals (error rate, latency, saturation, traffic) with fine-grained token-emission latency SLIs and a visualization of the hybrid admit controller (low-latency fast-path + regional fallback). This ticket covers the instrumentation spec, the metrics schema, a Grafana dashboard prototype, and a short playbook for oncall to interpret and triage admission-related incidents.

Why: our current dashboards surface request-level p95/p99 and high-level admission counts but do not make it easy to correlate regional admission hysteresis with token emission slowdowns or KV cache miss storms. Operators need one-pane views that show when load-shedding is protecting global SLOs and when it is regressing user-visible token emission latency.

Outcomes:
- A metrics schema for the hybrid admit controller including role (fast-path|fallback), admit decision reason, admit latency, kv_cache_hit, and per-token emission_latency histogram buckets.
- A Grafana dashboard with panels that let engineers pivot between region, shard, model-variant, and priority class.
- Automated baseline calculation for token-emission SLI and an alert recipe for drift/failure modes (e.g., KV miss surge, admission spike, token tail growth).
acceptance_criteria: Metrics schema published in the observability repo and merged (metrics.yml) with naming conventions: ri.admit.role, ri.admit.decision, ri.admit.latency_ms, ri.kv.hit, ri.token.emission_latency_ms

Grafana dashboard created and linked in the observability dashboards folder with at least 8 panels: global overview, regional admit waterfall, token emission heatmap, kv-hit correlation, admission reason breakdown, request vs token-latency scatter, SLI trend and burn rate, and playbook quick-links

Synthetic workload exercise demonstrates that when we trigger regional load-shedding the dashboard shows the admit decision transition and token emission SLI remains within defined SLO bands or an alert fires
Oncall playbook doc added with run steps, expected panel interpretations, and escalation paths
Unit/Integration tests for metric aggregation and histogram bucketing added to the telemetry test suite
implementation_notes: Add new tags to existing admit/span traces: region, shard_id, model_variant, priority_class, admit_role (fast|fallback), admit_reason
Use exponential histogram for ri.token.emission_latency_ms with buckets tuned for 0.5ms -> 2s so we capture emission tail without blowing cardinality
Emit a kv.cache_hit boolean counter per request and correlate with token emission 95/99 via backend rollup job
Aggregate admit counts by reason and region at 10s resolution; keep raw events for 7d and 1m rollups for 90d
Dashboard templating: region, model_variant, priority_class, time_window to allow fast pivoting during incidents
dashboard_panels: Global golden signal overview (error rate, request latency p50/p95/p99, CPU/GPU utilization)
Regional admit waterfall: per-region admit_rate broken down by role (fast|fallback) and reason
Token emission heatmap: per-token-index median and p99 across recent window
KV hit correlation panel: scatter of kv_hit_ratio vs token_emission_p99 by shard
Admission reason donut: percent of admits by reason (circuit_open, capacity_shed, admission_threshold)
Request vs token-latency scatter: request p99 mapped to token p99 to spot divergence
SLI trend and burn rate: token-emission-SLI (p95 <= 80ms) with burn chart
Playbook quick-links and suggested remediation checklist embedded as text panel
playbook_snippet: If token-emission p95 increases concurrently with admit.fallback rate: 1) check regional capacity dashboards and recent autoscale events; 2) inspect kv_cache hit ratio and recent cache-eviction spikes; 3) if KV misses > 30% in last 5m, escalate to runtime team and follow KV prefretch mitigation; 4) if admit_reason == capacity and GPU util < 60%, run admission hysteresis probe to detect misrouted traffic
